first_impression.reaction: I clicked through from a search for a hashtag generator, so I half expected a tool that doesn't exist. The intro tells me straight away I don't need one, which is honest. I went to the FAQ first like I always do, then skimmed back up. It's a hashtag article, not something that helps me pick a planner, so I read it fast.

journey.quote: You don't need a wedding hashtag generator to find one.
journey.reaction: Good. No bait and switch. The page admits up front there's no magic tool.

journey.section: How to make your own wedding hashtag
journey.quote: A website or chat assistant can hand you a long list, but the choosing and checking are yours.
journey.reaction: Fair and plain. It's honest about what a list can't do.

journey.quote: Sue and Ed joined as #sueed reads as "sued", which no couple wants on a welcome sign.
journey.reaction: This is the one practical check I'd actually use. Concrete example, not fluff.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Instagram's own rules for hashtags](https://help.instagram.com/351460621611097) allow numbers, but spaces and special characters such as $ or % won't work.
journey.reaction: Source and date. That's what I want. I can click it and check it myself.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: This is where it turns into a pitch. 'Anywhere in the world' and 'start to finish' are big promises with nothing behind them, dropped in the middle of an article about puns. And 'payments' makes me ask straight away: are you handling the money, and do you take a cut from the venue?

journey.quote: When people with private profiles tag posts, those posts won't appear publicly on hashtag pages.
journey.reaction: Useful, and it's the platform's own rule rather than an opinion. This is the bit I'd actually tell my fiancee about.

journey.quote: This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Honest about limits. Then it cites eSafety and the OAIC rather than making things up. I trust this section more than most wedding blogs.

journey.quote: The Act doesn't cover individuals, so it doesn't apply to a photo taken by someone acting in a personal capacity.
journey.reaction: Telling me the law probably doesn't help me here is the kind of uncomfortable fact marketing usually leaves out. Points for that.

journey.quote: Yes, as one option. A tag gives guests one place for public photos; for more privacy, pair it with a private album or skip it.
journey.reaction: Doesn't oversell the thing it's writing about. 'Or skip it' is an honest answer.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Fee in writing before work starts is the first thing on this page that speaks to me as a buyer. But it stops there. What is the fee based on? Flat, percentage, or baked into supplier prices? That's the question that decides whether I enquire.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor's fee worked out: flat fee, percentage of budget, or something else?
Do you take a commission or mark-up from venues or suppliers you book?
When the advisor 'plans the payments', does my money go through you or straight to the suppliers?
Is Wedded Concierge just an enquiry form, or does clicking it commit me to anything or cost anything?
Is there a real wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported sweeping claim, and a CTA in the middle of the article before any evidence about the service has been shown.

turn_offs_found.quote: Planning those events in another country is the bigger task.
turn_offs_found.why: Mild, but it's the pivot from helpful article to sales pitch. I can feel the upsell coming.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the privacy and children's photos section and the 'check where the names join' tip

cta_reaction.quote: Tell us your date, your guest list and where you would like to marry, and begin with [Wedded Concierge](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-hashtag-generator&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: Not from a hashtag article. The page gives me no reason to pick this planner over the other two I'm comparing. The 'fee in writing' line is a start, but until I know the fee model and whether you take a cut from suppliers, I'm not handing over my date and guest list. I might look at the Concierge page later out of curiosity, but I wouldn't enquire from here.

top_3_changes: Cut the sweeping promise in the mid-article plug ('anywhere in the world', 'from start to finish'). Say plainly what the advisor does without the superlatives.
In the closing section, give me a prompt to ask about how the fee is worked out and about supplier commissions, so the 'fee in writing' line points somewhere instead of stopping short.
Keep the sourced, dated Instagram, eSafety and OAIC lines exactly as they are. They are the reason I trusted the page at all.

suggested_edits.old: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
suggested_edits.new: A Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact.
suggested_edits.why: Removes unsupported superlatives. Adds nothing new.

suggested_edits.old: Tell us your date, your guest list and where you would like to marry, and begin with
suggested_edits.new: Ask how the fee is worked out and whether any supplier pays a commission, then tell us your date, your guest list and where you would like to marry, and begin with
suggested_edits.why: Invites the exact question a sceptical buyer has without stating any fee, commission policy or business detail.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic) using his voice and priorities
No invented brand facts; missing fee and commission details listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, names, statistics, business details, tool claims or real couples' tags
No more than 3 suggested edits and 3 top changes

assumptions: Daniel arrived from a Google search for 'wedding hashtag generator' while already comparing planners; low relevance reflects the topic, not a flaw in the article.
Persona card is provisional and not CRM-calibrated (weight 0.10).

open_questions.question: Should the second suggested edit (prompting readers to ask about fees and commissions) go to Nic for sign-off, since it nudges the fee conversation even though it states no fee model?
